claims: Since 1 July 2022, all employees receive super regardless of monthly earnings.
whys: 'All employees' is too broad. Employees under 18 still get SG only if they work more than 30 hours in a week.

claims: Since Payday Super commenced on 1 July 2026 ... within 7 business days
whys: The values are right but typed in by hand. The same values exist as SUPER_GUARANTEE.paydaySuperStart and SUPER_GUARANTEE_CHARGE.current.businessDaysToPay (lib/constants/australian-tax.ts:153, 172), and line 189 of the same file already uses the constant.

claims: A $100,000 'including super' role provides $89,286 salary and $10,714 super. The difference in base pay is $10,714.
whys: These figures are typed by hand rather than computed with calculateSuper or SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate, unlike the other figures nearby. They will go stale if the SG rate changes.

claims: Division 293 applies above $250,000 and adds 15% (30% total)
whys: The threshold and rate are typed by hand, with no constant and no source on this page.

claims: Hardcoded '15%' contributions tax, '45%' top marginal rate and '12% of OTE' (lines 118, 123, 124, 132, 141)
'Sacrificing this full amount saves you tax at your marginal rate minus the 15% contributions tax.'
whys: These figures are typed into the prose and table instead of coming from constants, so they will drift when a rate changes. The hero on the same page already uses SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate.
This leaves out the Medicare levy, which the /salary-sacrifice-calculator/ FAQ counts in the saving. It is also untrue below the tax-free threshold and under Division 293, and the 15% is hardcoded.

claims: Table cell: 'Tax saving at $100K salary: $1,500 per $10,000 sacrificed'
whys: $1,500 is only 30% minus 15%. It leaves out the 2% Medicare levy, so it is $1,700. The /salary-sacrifice-calculator/ hero and FAQ count the Medicare levy in the saving, so the two pages disagree. The figure is also hardcoded.
constants: Derive from TAX_BRACKETS[2].rate, MEDICARE_LEVY.rate and CONTRIBUTIONS_TAX_RATE (lib/constants/super-contributions)
